name: Dynamic DNS
overview: Keep your DNS records pointed at your server's current public IP.
description: Dynamic DNS keeps one or more DNS records pointed at your Jellyfin server's current public IP. It runs in-process as a scheduled task and updates Cloudflare, DuckDNS, or any dyndns2-compatible provider over outbound HTTP/S.

versions.changelog:
## Fixed
- The plain-http warning no longer logs the request URL's authority, which carried the update secret into the server log for providers whose credential lives in the URL's userinfo (ClouDNS DynURL, Directnic gateway URL). The warning now names the record's hostname instead
- A Data Protection key store that fails for an unexpected reason surfaces instead of being silently downgraded to plaintext credential storage; the expected failures (bad path, no permission, no service) still fall back as before

## Developer
- Address the outstanding CodeQL findings across the plugin and test projects (LINQ filtering and projection, ternary assignment, dictionary lookup, response disposal in the HTTP test stub)

## Fixed
- Resolve the TTL "1 = automatic" sentinel to a per-provider default instead of sending a literal one-second TTL (Gandi, GoDaddy, Spaceship, Hetzner, DNSExit)
- Yandex matches records by type as well as name, so an IPv4 update can no longer overwrite an AAAA or TXT record, and A/AAAA now update independently
- Spaceship writes the new record before removing stale ones, so a failed update leaves the old address serving instead of deleting the record
- Hetzner treats an accepted, still-applying action as success instead of timing out and counting a false failure toward backoff
- DNS Made Easy treats "no update required" as success instead of walking a healthy record into backoff
- DDNS.fm validates the response body instead of treating any HTTP 200 as success
- NS1 record creation sends the required zone, domain, and type fields, so first-time setup works
- Apex hostnames infer the correct domain when no zone is set (Porkbun, Dynadot, Spaceship, Dinahosting), and Dinahosting gained an optional Zone field
- OVH DynHost, DynDNS v1, DSLReports, and NearlyFreeSpeech.NET declare IPv4-only, so an IPv6 address is no longer recorded as pushed and endlessly re-pushed
- A record with one working address family is no longer paused by backoff when only the other family fails

## Developer
- Harden the publish workflow (release body via env, tag-derived version, fail-fast asset downloads, required tag on manual dispatch)
- Slash-command dispatch uses the JF_BOT_TOKEN secret instead of a placeholder
- CI packages with build.sh and verifies the zip contents, and build.sh parses build.yaml colon- and space-safely
- Response-parsing tests for every provider plus orchestrator and API tests

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12
- Use ActivityLogger from Base 2026.7.12
- Use BackoffPolicy from Base 2026.7.12

## Feature
- Output logging to Activity Logs for better visibility

## Security
- Encrypt credentials saved through the generic plugin configuration endpoint instead of waiting for the next run
- Warn in the log when a record updates over plain http
- Show a dashboard warning when credential encryption is unavailable and secrets are stored in plaintext

## Developer
- Share one SecretProtector between the dashboard and generic save paths
- Snapshot the configuration per update run instead of mutating live records

## Fixes
- Prune record status against fresh record ids so a record added mid-run is not dropped

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.6.23
- Fix encryption of tokens to ensure they will not break between versions
- Migrate everything so it lives in the provider for ease of maintenance
- Reorganize files

## Documentation
- Creates Provider documentation per ddclient

## Fixes
- Check the DNS for current IP instead of always resending
- If the current DNS is internal, use the previous IP sent (previous behavior)

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.6.19
- Fix encryption of tokens to ensure they will not break between versions

## Initial release

This plugin acts as a DDNS resolver using Jellyfin as its host. A lot of this work will look very similar to [ddclient](https://github.com/ddclient/ddclient) which was a huge help and inspiration for this plugin. This takes the work they've taken and wraps it into a Jellyfin plugin for server owners don't want to manage more than one application.
